tool: Citation check that flags citations which do not resolve
checked: POST /research/cite-check with cl._post canned. A status-200 citation with one cluster renders 'resolved' and a status-404 citation renders 'not found, verify before filing'; the Note written to the matter carries both lines and the counts. Then the same with a status-300 (ambiguous) citation.
notes: FIXED. Ambiguous results are reported as ambiguous with their candidates listed, distinct from not found. Both still say verify before filing. | Audit note: An ambiguous citation (CourtListener status 300, several candidate clusters) is reported as 'not found, verify before filing' rather than as ambiguous, while the same table row still prints one candidate case name and a working CourtListener link, so the row contradicts itself; the matter Note records it as 'not found' too. _courtlistener.citation_lookup sets found = (status == 200 and clusters), so status 300 makes found False, and cite_check.html only shows the 'N possible matches' badge when found and ambiguous are both true. That branch is therefore only reachable on a status 200 with more than one cluster. The error is in the safe direction (nothing is wrongly marked good), so it is a mislabel, not a bad-cite risk.

B','date_filed':'2000-01-01','absolute_url':'/opinion/1/a/'},{'id':2,'case_name':'C v. D','date_filed':'2001-01-01','absolute_url':'/opinion/2/c/'}]}], then POST /research/cite-check with text='See 1 X. 1.' and matter_id set. tool: Settlement disbursement worksheet with trust postings
checked: Gross $100,000.00 at 33.33% with two matter expenses ($1,250.00 + $325.50), one typed extra cost ($402.00) and two unpaid liens ($8,000.00 + $2,500.00). Every stored line matched to the cent: fee 3333000, costs 197750, liens 1050000, other 0, net 5419250, and fee+costs+liens+other+net == gross. PDF shows the same figures and 'Balanced.'. Disburse without funds was refused with no trust rows written and the worksheet left approved. Disburse with 'record the settlement deposit' wrote 6 trust rows summing to exactly 0 (matter trust balance 0), the net row is -5419250 to the client, both liens flipped to paid and the worksheet is disbursed. A negative net is refused at approve and at disburse.
notes: FIXED. Costs default to expenses not yet billed to the client; already-billed ones show unticked with the invoice named, any row can be flipped, and the counted ids are stored on the worksheet. | Audit note: compute_worksheet deducts every Expense row on the matter with no regard to whether it has already been invoiced to and paid by the client, and the worksheet form offers no way to exclude one (only to add extra costs). On a hybrid or hourly-plus-contingency matter where case costs were billed and collected, the same cost is taken out of the client's settlement a second time and the net to client is wrong by that amount, with no correction available in the UI. The pure-contingency path the module is aimed at is unaffected.
repro: On a matter with a $1,250.00 expense, set that Expense.invoice_id to a real invoice (i.e. bill and collect it), then call app.blueprints.pi.compute_worksheet(matter, 1000000, 0). The already-invoiced expense is still in d['expenses'] and still in d['costs'], so net is 125000 cents light. /pi/<id> has no per-expense exclude control (no 'expense_id' or exclude checkbox in the settlement form).

checked: Built the conditions for nine rules on one matter (records requested 90 days ago and not received, records in with no bills request, an open lien with no contact, stage=demand with no policy limits, a limitations date 45 days out with no deadline task, a demand sent 45 days ago with no offer, a 60-day treatment gap between two confirmed entries, an MRI mention with no imaging visit, and no activity for 30 days). Run one produced exactly one finding per (kind, key) with the expected severities (missing_records and sol_near high, treatment_gap and limits_unknown medium, bills_missing and lien_no_contact low) and the limitations message carried the right date and 'in 45 days'. POST /audit/run, /audit and /audit/<matter_id> all render, and `python -m app.cli case_audit` runs. A canned AI reply with an invalid kind and an invalid severity was coerced into the AI_KIND_KEYS/SEVERITIES enums and stored with origin=ai.

tool: Email filing to matters (IMAP)
checked: Three RFC 822 messages built with email.message and pushed through run_emailin with the IMAP fetch replaced. Matching by bracketed matter number ([M-1001]) and by sender email to a client with exactly one open matter both worked; a third from an unknown sender landed unfiled. Both attachments of the first mail became Documents in the Email folder with tag email, and the bytes on disk match the stored size. Re-running the same fetch returned filed 0 / unfiled 0 / skipped 3 with no new Message or Document rows. /messages/unfiled lists the unmatched mail and its held attachment; filing it by hand moved the mail to the matter, stored the held file as a Document and removed the hold directory. With IMAP unset, imap_configured() is False, fetch_unseen() returns [] and `python -m app.cli emailin` says nothing to do.
notes: The live IMAP leg (fetch_unseen against a real server) was not exercised; it needs an IMAP account. Everything downstream of it was tested with parsed dicts, which is how the module is designed to be tested. Caveat: idempotence is keyed only on Message-ID, so a mail with no Message-ID header re-fetched twice is filed twice with duplicate Documents. In practice IMAP marks the message seen so a second fetch does not happen, and almost every MTA supplies a Message-ID.

tool: Document automation from DOCX and HTML templates
checked: DOCX path: a real python-docx template with {{ client_name }}, {{ matter_number }}, {{ firm_name }} and a plain {CLIENT_NAME} field uploaded through /doctemplates/new, then generated for a matter. The output .docx was opened as a zip and word/document.xml read: the client display name and the matter number are both substituted and no {{ }} is left. A merge field deliberately split across two Word runs ('{{ cli' + 'ent_name }}') also substitutes correctly. HTML path: a template generated to PDF, read back with pypdf, has the client name and matter number substituted and no {{ }} left; the Document is stored with mime application/pdf under folder Generated and both outputs carry extracted_text so they are searchable.
notes: FIXED. Plain {FIELD} merge fields are converted before rendering, including fields split across Word runs, and any field that could not be filled is named on the page. | Audit note: Plain {FIELD} merge fields are detected but never substituted. detect_fields_text matches a second syntax, (?<!{){([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{1,60})}(?!}), so a template containing {CLIENT_NAME} lists CLIENT_NAME as a merge field and the generate page renders an input named f_CLIENT_NAME for it. Neither renderer can fill it: render_docx uses docxtpl and render_html_pdf uses Jinja, and both only expand {{ ... }}. Whatever the user types in that box is silently discarded and the literal {CLIENT_NAME} is left in the delivered document. This is the syntax most Word merge templates arrive in, so it is a likely first-use failure.
repro: Build a .docx containing the line 'Plain style field: {CLIENT_NAME}', upload it at /doctemplates/new with kind=docx, then GET /doctemplates/<id>/generate?matter_id=<m> (the form shows an input named f_CLIENT_NAME) and POST to generate. Unzip the output and read word/document.xml: it still contains the literal {CLIENT_NAME}. Same with an HTML template containing {CLIENT_NAME}.
